entry_points.kicker: A small place with a long shadow

supporting_claims.statement: Jura makes legal hierarchy, grape identity and winemaking method unusually easy to compare in one small place: Chardonnay and Savagnin whites, three red grapes, vin jaune, sparkling wine and mistelle all coexist without meaning the same thing.

entry_points.title: Why does Jura feel bigger than it is?

supporting_claims.statement: Savagnin is a wine grape, not a cellar method. CARTA's primary sources separately document it in topped, non-oxidative wine, Jura's sous-voile and vin-jaune context, and sparkling-wine rules, so the grape name alone does not tell you how the wine was raised.

entry_points.title: Savagnin is a grape, not a style

entry_points.kicker: The outlines are telling different truths

supporting_claims.statement: Arbois, Côtes du Jura, L’Etoile and Château-Chalon are geographic AOPs; Crémant du Jura and Macvin du Jura overlap that geography but govern different wine categories and methods.

entry_points.title: Why do Jura's wine areas overlap?

supporting_claims.statement: Plantgrape reports published genetic analyses indicating Petit Manseng is closely related to Savagnin; this is a closeness claim, not a resolved parent-offspring statement in the evidence captured here.
